+name: baseline-drift
+
+# Guards the committed scanctl baseline (.scanctl/baseline.sarif) against rot.
+# security.yml suppresses the baselined findings so per-PR code scanning stays
+# clean; this job re-scans WITHOUT the baseline and fails if the live findings
+# no longer match what the baseline claims -- either a stale entry (a suppressed
+# finding disappeared) or a new finding the baseline does not cover. Runs on
+# dependency/config changes, weekly (upstream rule packs shift on their own),
+# and on demand.
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    paths:
+      - 'package-lock.json'
+      - 'package.json'
+      - 'renovate.json'
+      - '.scanctl/**'
+      - '.github/workflows/baseline-drift.yml'
+  schedule:
+    - cron: '37 7 * * 1'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  drift:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0 # full history so gitleaks scans past commits (parity with security.yml)
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - name: Set up Go
+        uses: actions/setup-go@4a3601121dd01d1626a1e23e37211e3254c1c06c # v6

GitHub Actions step uses a mutable tag or branch reference. Tags and branch names can be silently repointed by the action owner, enabling supply-chain attacks — as seen in the trivy-action and kics-github-action compromises. Pin the reference to a full 40-character commit SHA instead, e.g. `uses: actions/checkout@8ade135a41bc03ea155e62e844d188df1ea18608`.

[Show more details](https://github.com/catenahq/docs/security/code-scanning/143)
